beats.t: As the ferry reached midriver, Yeoni opened her palm again. Night wind slipped between five fingers that still didn't feel like hers.
You should rest, too. You've been holding yourself up on that hurt paw.
Yeongnyangi stumbled as he shifted seats. She instinctively supported his little paw, and 庚 warmed on her wrist.
Wait. Don't let go.

Light spread along every white hair and enfolded his small body. Four marks beneath his hat brightened in turn, then sank toward his wrist. In her hand, his little paw slowly lengthened from its pink pads.
[ 庚 · Connection restored / Physical form restored ]
As the light receded, a silver-haired man sat on the boat's floor. His little navy cloak had lengthened into a silver coat embroidered in gold. What Yeoni held was now a human hand.
...Yeongnyangi?
It's me. In this form, use the name you gave me. Neo.
He flexed unfamiliar fingers. The rust-colored mark still spread across the back of his left hand, even on human skin.
Your hand is warm. Does it still hurt?
A little. Becoming human doesn't heal everything.
Yeoni made room. Neo folded unfamiliar knees and sat. For the first time, their shoulders touched at the same height.
Then let's get used to it slowly. I only just came back, too.
Yes. I'll borrow your shoulder today.
Moka finally woke and looked between them, rubbing both eyes twice and smoothing whiskers once.
The cat was human? First the pig, now him. Am I the only animal left on this boat?
Despite the grumbling, Moka draped a blanket over Neo's shoulders.
Explain after breakfast. You're both shaking.
When Yeoni laughed, Neo smiled faintly too. His face was strange, but he still looked away when embarrassed. Only then did her grip on his hand ease.
The boat followed the river all night. At dawn, the familiar dock of the time-selling island appeared. The smell of baking drifted from the alley.
Sis, come quick! Guests! No, not guests!
Luna!
Huh? Pig Lady's voice, but a human face?
It's Pig Sis. Now Human Sis.
Wow, a real person! You've got fingers, so you can pick up bread!
Luna seized Yeoni's hand and shook it, then felt each finger in wonder.
Then her eyes stopped on the silver-haired man behind Yeoni. A white hair clung to the hem of his silver coat.
Wait. Where's Cat Guy? Don't tell me the cat was human?
Asked the same thing on the boat. Never got an answer.
A cat too. Just not right now.
Then where's your tail? Your whiskers?
Luna lifted his coat hem to search for a tail. Neo froze and looked at Yeoni. She turned away to contain her laughter.
He wants to be called Neo in this form. I haven't found the tail either.
Luna, finish with the dough before you play. Oh, our guests.
Luna's sister emerged with flour on her apron. She looked them over one by one, then gave a smile like a sigh.
Even Neo is human now. I'll be surprised later. Show me your arms and tails first.
Though I'm so used to it. May I still call you Mr. Cat?
My tail always looks like this!
Everyone inside. Wash, sit, eat. In that order.
The bakery was warm. Fresh loaves steamed across the shelves, and the wall clock finally kept its own time.
Today's first batch. No charge, but you must finish it.
It has every smell. The smell of something with flavor.
Hands to eat with now. It's hot, so take it slowly.
I know. But it smells so good, I can hardly wait.
Luna offered Yeoni buttered bread. It slipped through her fingers and fell butter-side down.
Huh? Again! I'll get another!
The second and third pieces landed the same way. Moka's bread and Neo's bread were perfectly fine.
My lady, an empty luck balance shows up in little things. Take the whole plate next time.
Luna's sister set bread on a plate before her. Yeoni bit into it and went still. Warm bread, melted butter slowly sweetening her tongue.
It's good.
Are you crying? Too hot?
I don't know. The ledger took all my luck, but apparently left the flavor.
Luna's sister silently added another piece. Yeoni ate it and kept crying. No one laughed.
It can take your fortune, but not your appetite. That belongs to your body.
Then Luna's sister returned to the oven. Her back was a little more bent than before. Not all the time she'd sold had come back.
May I ask your birth date and time? With bread this good, your Eating God must be excellent.
Fortune-teller, keep your mouth shut while eating bread. House rules.
Yes. I like rules.
I like that rule.
As the others drifted away, full, Yeoni took a bread bag to the back steps. Neo sat beside her and tugged down his left sleeve, but the rust stain on his hand wasn't entirely hidden.
Don't hide it. I've seen it all now.
Neo hesitated, then rolled up his sleeve. The rust stopped below his shoulder. A changed form hadn't erased the wounds.
I take back telling you to step aside. That's what I went to the river to say.
I know. I heard.
You heard? Where?
Downstream. Your voice was louder than the water.
Why remember that?
I'll promise too. If it hurts, I'll tell you instead of hiding it.
A promise. Customer Support loses stars for breaking promises.
Agreed. Don't put out your fire either. We'll hold on together until the water thaws.
She tore off bread and put it in his mouth. He didn't refuse. They chewed in silence for a while.
Neo's gaze rested on the flower pin in her hair. The flower that had grown on her head remained a small pin in human form. Of its five petals, one was still paper-white.
Guess this isn't coming back. It's okay. The pin's pretty.
Back inside, Luna was already racing around with dough for the next batch.
Beside the oven, Moka transferred embers into a little earthenware jar. Every movement of the tongs singed whisker tips.
What's that jar? For baking?
An ember jar. They say all the festival island's ovens went out. I'm taking some fire back.
Keep the lid on and it'll last three days. Don't open it on the way.
Moka cradled the jar and pressed the lid twice, wearing a different face from the one used for talking about skewers.
The sun rose higher. Plate in hand, Yeoni went to the window. A few cats, drawn by the smell of bread, dozed on the quiet alley wall.
A black shape sat beneath the opposite eaves. Through a torn cloak, a black ring showed around its right forepaw.
(The tiger.)
The tiger wasn't looking at the bakery. It was pretending not to. Only the tip of its nose tilted ever so slightly toward the bread.
Yeoni began opening the window, then stopped. If she went outside, the tiger would leave. That much she felt sure of.
What are you looking at?
Oh, no. Just someone outside.
Luna's sister glanced through the window. Without a word, she wrapped a fresh roll in paper and went out.
The alley was cooler than the bakery. As Luna's sister approached the eaves, the tiger rose, water dripping from her cloak.
I'm only passing through.
Of course. Passing through hungry.
Luna's sister offered bread. The tiger looked at it, then at her face, eyes calculating what she was buying, at what price, and when it must be repaid.
How much is this?
Free.
Nothing is free.
Something is. One thing, right here.
The tiger didn't reach out; Luna's sister didn't wait. She opened the tiger's paw herself, set the bread inside, then closed it so the bread wouldn't fall.
Eat it warm. Once it cools, it's just bread.
She turned and went back inside. Not once did she look back.
The tiger stood there a long time. The bread was warm in her paw. The black ring stayed still, as though it had forgotten to tighten.
Free, you say?
She didn't eat it. Carefully, she tucked it inside her torn cloak beside the drummer child's name, then vanished into the shade.
Back in the bakery, Luna's sister resumed kneading as though nothing had happened.
Thank you.
For what? A bakery is a place that gives people bread.
Yeoni added nothing. The eaves outside stood empty. The wet marks didn't dry until the sun began to sink.
Toward evening, light leaked through the old storeroom door. At first it looked like oven light, but it spread along the cracks in golden threads.
Sis, the storeroom door's glowing! Another time thief?
That door never opens.
The old woodgrain became a card's design. Stars filled the border, an open door appeared at its center, and words rose below in place of a number.
[ THE DOOR · Destiny code 8/8 confirmed · Return available · Companions restricted ]
[ Opens: dawn tomorrow / Companion: one borrowed space ]
I know this. The first card I saw in the app. I tapped it and came here.
A door home. Only someone with all eight characters, and whoever borrows their space, may pass.
Then I can go? Home?
If you choose. It opens tomorrow morning. The door decides where it leads.
Yeoni stepped toward it, stopped, and turned. Moka, Yundal, Luna, Luna's sister. And Neo.
We're all going together, right?
No one answered at once. Yundal quietly held his gloved hand toward the door. The golden threads broke off before it.
[ Year □□ · Month □□ · Day □□ · Hour ■■ · 7/8 · Entry denied ]
As expected, not me. No hour.
Your hour? The one Blue Rabbit ate?
To this door, missing one of eight characters means I'm not quite a finished person. Rather hurtful.
Then we'll find it. Find it together, then leave together.
You're willing to wait for me, my lady. Proof we're compatible.
No.
Yundal smiled. The smile took a little too long to end.
I'm not going, either.
Moka?
I'm an otter from this side to begin with. I've got to take these embers to the festival island and keep the fire.
Besides, bring a skewer-grilling otter to the human world. Straight onto the news.
But still.
No buts. One less person to hear my rap. That's the only shame.
Don't cry, human. You're uglier than you were as a pig.
Saying that, Moka tucked the ember jar under one arm and bumped a forehead against Yeoni's hand, as on the day they'd shared breath.
Then Neo...
I'm going.
Why?
I'm a borrowed space. Where the space goes, I follow. Customer service makes house calls too.
How many stars for the house-call service?
Five. You said so on the river.
You heard even that.
The door's golden light lowered, awaiting her answer. Going meant leaving these people. Staying meant the day left in her room would remain suspended.
I'll go. But I want to sleep here tonight first.
Then I'll get the blankets out. I'll bake early tomorrow.
The bakery lights stayed on late. Yeoni pulled a borrowed blanket to her chin and watched the storeroom's golden light for a long time.
Next morning, Yeoni and Neo stood before the door. Luna pressed a bread bag into her arms; her sister only waved from the oven.
Come back. Human Lady or Pig Lady, I don't care. Just come again.
I will. Next time I'll pay for the bread myself.
If it's not as good as ours, we won't accept it.
My lady, things here may blur like a dream on the other side. Don't worry too much, though.
They won't blur. How could I forget bread this good?
Of course. You can't forget bread.
He put his gloved hand in his pocket. He didn't mention that Luna's sister had asked his name again that morning.
Yeoni took the handle. It was warm as fresh bread. When the door opened, a golden morning wind poured through.
As she crossed the threshold, she thought she heard something behind her. Yundal murmuring a name other than his own. The wind covered it.
The door closed. Those left in the bakery watched it for a while. It was an old storage door again.
Where no one could see, raindrops slipped through the closed door's crack, as if following someone to the other side.
